name: sums_diffs
engineering_invariants: Clamp every time-derived progress/fraction to [0.0, 1.0] before fractional powers or annealing schedules; an expensive score call may cross a deadline after the loop condition was checked.
Before randrange(start, stop) or equivalent dynamic sampling, prove or guard that stop > start; unchanged/clamped parameters may otherwise make the range empty.
Never encode a conjectured theoretical limit as a finite candidate score; research narrative remains unverified unless the trusted evaluator emits a bounded or formal verdict.
A formal proof term may target only a typed claim with a normalized rational target; candidate text, theorem names, imports, status, and axioms are never trusted.
When a trusted obligation is refuted, preserve the minimal counterexample and revise the construction or claim instead of hiding the failed obligation.
fallback_directions: Refine near the current best: small perturbations of the best known set or its generating parameters. Exploitation, not exploration.
Try known MSTD (more-sums-than-differences) base sets and asymmetric variants.
Structured constructions: unions of arithmetic progressions / intervals with carefully chosen gaps.
Base expansion / product constructions with mixed base sets at different digit positions.
Search for a small modular sum-difference gadget, record a standalone trusted modular_sum_diff certificate, and state any broader claim separately as unverified.
Use repeated digit products to infer a carry/borrow recurrence or finite-state model, then state the smallest exact experiment that could refute it.
Test whether a promising local gadget composes through rows, columns, products, or CRT; separate the finite observation from the claimed parameterized family.
Adversarially test the strongest unverified research claim in the Experience Bank and preserve a minimal counterexample or bounded certificate.
Randomized local search: add/remove/shift elements, keep changes that raise C(A).
Scale promising constructions while preserving sum dominance and keeping exact verification within the evaluator budgets.
Combine the best ideas seen so far in the experience bank.
